Lakhveer Singh Alias Pintu --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Prateek Tripathi, learned counsel
for the applicant through Legal Aid.
2. Mr. Vijay Khanduri, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
3. The instant bail application is moved
on behalf of the applicant Lakhveer Singh @
Pintu, S/o Mangat Singh who is praying for
bail in reference to FIR dated 02.04.2023
bearing FIR No. 95 of 2023 P.S. Rajpur
District Dehradun wherein the present
applicant along with co-accused Jaitunisa
(wife of the deceased) have been implicated
and charge sheeted for the offences
punishable under Sections 302, 201 and 34
IPC.
4. It is argued by the learned counsel for
the applicant that the present applicant has
been implicated only on a presumption that
he was having illicit relations with the wife
of the deceased and both of them conspired
and commit the offence and killed the
deceased by strangulation. He submits that
there are in total 11 prosecution witnesses
and up till date 7 prosecution witnesses have
been examined and the present applicant is
languishing in jail since last more than three
years, i.e. w.e.f. 02.04.2023, however, the trial
has yet not been expedited so far. With
regard to the co-accused (wife of the
deceased) learned counsel submits that her

bail application is already rejected by the
Coordinate Bench. He also submits that the
applicant has already suffered long
incarceration of 3 years therefore he may be
enlarged on bail.
5. On the other side, Mr. Vijay Khanduri,
learned Brief Holder vehemently opposed
the bail application by submitting that there
are credible evidences against the applicant
and he actively participated in the
commission of crime along with the wife of
the deceased and in a well organized manner
they commit this crime. He further submits
that there is recovery of mobile of the
applicant from the place of the incident and
there is also a testimony of the eye witness
who is son of the deceased.
6. After hearing the submissions of the
learned counsel for the parties and taking
into consideration that trial is at concluding
stage since out of 11 prosecution witnesses
up till date 7 prosecution witnesses have
already been examined, therefore the trial
may be expedite shortly and, furthermore,
co- accused has already been denied bail by
the Coordinate Bench, therefore, this Court is
of the view that the applicant does not
deserve for bail but simultaneously the Trial
Court may be directed to expedite the trial.
7. In such view of the matter, the instant
bail application is rejected and the trial court
is directed to expedite the trial as early as
possible preferably within six months from
the date of receipt of copy of this order.
8. Registry is directed to send the copy of
this order to the concerned Trial Court for
taking necessary steps to expedite the trial.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
01-09-2026
Parul
